36 A battery of electromotive force (e.m.f.) 10 V and internal resistance r is connected to three
resistors of resistances R, 2.0 Ω and 15 Ω, as shown. A current of 0.45 A is in the resistor of
resistance 2.0 Ω and a current of 0.48 A is in the resistor of resistance 15 Ω.

hints: Notice the $15 \text{ }\Omega$ resistor with $0.48 \text{ A}$ is in parallel with the series combination of $R$ and the $2.0 \text{ }\Omega$ resistor with $0.45 \text{ A}$, so both branches share the same p.d.
Use $V = IR$ on the $15 \text{ }\Omega$ branch to get that common p.d., then set it equal to $0.45 \times (R + 2.0)$ to isolate $R$.
Add the two branch currents to get the current through internal resistance $r$, then use $E = Ir + V_{parallel}$ with $E = 10 \text{ V}$ to find $r$.
walkthrough: Identify the parallel part: the bottom branch is $15 \text{ }\Omega$ carrying $0.48 \text{ A}$ and the top branch is $R + 2.0 \text{ }\Omega$ carrying $0.45 \text{ A}$, so the p.d. across both branches is the same.
Calculate the common parallel p.d. from the known branch: $V_p = I \times R = 0.48 \times 15 = 7.2 \text{ V}$.
Apply the same $V_p$ to the top branch: $V_p = 0.45 \times (R + 2.0)$. So $R + 2.0 = 7.2 / 0.45 = 16 \text{ }\Omega$, giving $R = 14 \text{ }\Omega$.
Find the current supplied by the battery through $r$ using Kirchhoff current law at the junction: $I = 0.45 + 0.48 = 0.93 \text{ A}$.
Use the e.m.f. equation $E = Ir + V_p$ with $E = 10 \text{ V}$: $10 = 0.93 \times r + 7.2$. So $0.93 \times r = 2.8$ and $r = 2.8 / 0.93 \approx 3.0 \text{ }\Omega$.
The pair $r = 3.0 \text{ }\Omega$ and $R = 14 \text{ }\Omega$ matches the table. This is option A.

A.explanation: Parallel p.d. is $0.48 \times 15 = 7.2 \text{ V}$, giving $R = 14 \text{ }\Omega$ and $r = 3.0 \text{ }\Omega$ from the full $0.93 \text{ A}$ lost volts.

B.explanation: The $r = 3.0 \text{ }\Omega$ is correct but $R = 20 \text{ }\Omega$ gives $0.45 \times 22 = 9.9 \text{ V}$ across the top branch, not the $7.2 \text{ V}$ required.

C.explanation: The $R = 14 \text{ }\Omega$ is correct but $r = 5.8 \text{ }\Omega$ uses only the $0.48 \text{ A}$ current, ignoring the $0.45 \text{ A}$ branch when finding lost volts.

D.explanation: Both values fail the circuit equations since $R = 20 \text{ }\Omega$ breaks parallel p.d. equality and $r = 5.8 \text{ }\Omega$ ignores total current through $r$.
